pr_body:
Implements a recursive option for the `readdir` and `readdirSync` methods.

Closes: https://github.com/nodejs/node/issues/34992
Ref: https://github.com/nodejs/tooling/issues/130

---

Starting with tests to just get a sense for how things should behave. Will dive into the implementation next. Any feedback/concerns is welcome at any time.
pr_comments: @nodejs/tooling @bnb @bcoe
Can you fix linting please? It's hard to review with all the lint comments.  Thanks!

I am wondering if it wouldn't be nice for users to change the recursive option to be either `depth-first` or `breadth-first`. This would make the output and algorithm very clear:

```javascript
await fs.readdir('.', { recursive: 'breadth-first' }) // ['a', 'b', 'a/x']
await fs.readdir('.', { recursive: 'depth-first' }) // ['a', 'a/x', b']
await fs.readdir('.', { recursive: true }) // throw new Error('Specify recursive as either "breadth-first" or "depth-first")
```

> If we just return arrays, the process might crash after hours or so when the array allocations run into an out-of-memory situation, never having produced any results.

A `readdir` operation in itself doesn't expose how many entries may be returned and a huge folder takes a lot of time too. Having the API would make sense for a project that _kinda_ knows its content and can wait for the time.

Considering [`readdirp`](https://www.npmjs.com/package/readdirp) as prior art, would `fs.readdirp('.')` be a good name for a streaming API variant?

Thanks for all the great feedback folks. 

I'm going to update the tests to exemplify an API design for this feature that includes things like:
- stream result
- list of Dirent result
- option for DFS vs BFS

We also discussed on the call to keep this initial implementation simple. Omit things like a `filter` option (as shown in readdirp) since it does not already exist in the standard readdir.

I personally would like there to be some sort of default behavior when using just `{ recursive: true }`, but then maybe the option can also support more configuration like `{ recurisve: { algorithm: 'depth-first', returnType: 'stream' } }`.

> I personally would like there to be some sort of default behavior when using just { recursive: true }, but then maybe the option can also support more configuration like { recurisve: { algorithm: 'depth-first', returnType: 'stream' } }

I would prefer to also see `{ recursive: true}` Just Work™. Perhaps additional options could be allowed, if people _really really_ want to have that more granular control?

Summary of recent updates:

Default case uses just `{ recursive: true }`. This will return an array of strings in a random order. 

I included examples with the `withFileTypes` option enabled i.e. `{ recursive: true, withFileTypes: true }` which will output an array of `fs.Dirent` objects in a random order.

I included another way to configure the `recursive` property using an object with two optional properties:

```ts
{
  result?: 'stream',
  algorithm?: 'depth-first' | 'breadth-first'
}
```

Unless folks can come up with another `result` option, I'm going to change that property to just `stream?: boolean`.

I did **not** update the promise tests - want to focus on the API shape for now.

I did **not** include async tests for all of the sync operations. After API agreement I'll add those in.

I did **not** include error case tests yet. Will think about that more later

When implementing [a readdir stream a while back](https://github.com/martinheidegger/dat-readdir-stream) I had to do `.stat` calls to figure out if an entry is a directory or not. The other data from the stat operation was very useful in the display of the content, and was returned by the API as well. Same is possible in `readdirp` by supplying [the `alwaysStat` option](https://github.com/paulmillr/readdirp#options). Maybe it would be worth considering it here as well?

Different thing: Would it be a good idea to support abort signals?

> Same is possible in readdirp by supplying the alwaysStat option. Maybe it would be worth considering it here as well?

If i'm not mistaken the `withFileTypes` option semi-covers this use case. I don't want to deviate too much from the rest of the fs api at least for the first implementation.

> Would it be a good idea to support abort signals?

Yes, for the async operations we could do this

After some consideration, I think supporting alternative algorithms is going to make this PR more complicated than I can handle at this time. 

What would be the best way to defer the algorithm feature of this PR? One option: I can put the test files I've written for them into a new branch and open an issue to track. @bcoe @bnb
imo getting a basic implementation in and expanding on that with additional algorithms in later PRs would be fine.
See linked issue #41709 for `algorithm` feature
Also for the sake of initial implementation, I'm dropping the promise API. I'd like to see us land the sync/async versions and then progress from there
@Ethan-Arrowood What about the concerns raised in https://github.com/nodejs/node/pull/41439#pullrequestreview-847231885 and https://github.com/nodejs/node/pull/41439#pullrequestreview-847288542 ?

Ahh I missed those somehow. 

My initial thought on the discussion is it seems like a fine idea. Focus on a stream based recursive readdir, and then also add a recursive option to opendir that would return an array.

Okay new API design for initial implementation:

- Add new `boolean` option `recursive` to `readdir` and `readdirSync`
- The result is a `Readable` stream of the paths in the directory
- The `fs.promises.readdir` version will return an async iterator

Future work:
- Add `recursive` option to `opendir`
- Add additional options to `recursive` option such as:
  - `algorithm` which specifies how to traverse the directory graph
  - `return` which specifies what to return (`array`, `stream`)
    - this can be used in conjunction with `withFileTypes` in order to return an array of `Dirents`

What do we think?

> The result is a Readable stream of the paths in the directory

Does it mean that `readdir` and `readdirSync` would return exactly the same thing?
Good catch. I meant that the callback will be passed the same readable that is returned by the sync version

> Good catch. I meant that the callback will be passed the same readable that is returned by the sync version

Would anything really async happen before the stream is constructed and returned in the callback version?

Not sure. I guess it'd be the difference between opendir and opendirSync under the hood. 

The promise version of this is simple, I plan on using an async iterable.

The sync and callback versions I haven't given tooo much thought beyond implementing a Readable and using _read to exhaust recursive calls to something.
Then why don't we make `opendir` optionally recursive? It seems to me that it would make the API more consistent

Ah i may be lost now. opendir just returns a Dir (via callback, promise, or sync) that's an async iterable of Dirents. Are you suggesting that when recursive is enabled, the async iterable will return everything in it as Dirents?
I think that's what I'm suggesting, yes.

Makes sense! I spent the majority of my flight taking a crack at this. I'm getting close. It primarily has to do with the `Dir` class. Essentially, one implementation for `Dir.readSync` and another for `Dir.read`. The async iterator aspect of `Dir` utilizes a promisified `Dir.read` method under the hood

Just pushed some changes to `opendirSync`, `Dir`, and `readdirSync`.

As @targos and i discussed above, the changes in `Dir` are useful for `readdirSync` as well as for `opendirSync`. I anticipate similar changes to the non-sync parts of `Dir` will be perfect for `readdir`, `opendir`, and the respective promise versions. 

Stuff is a little sloppy but it ✨ works ✨ so i'm going to move forward with the async/callback stuff and then we can iterate on making it better

> Also for the sake of initial implementation, I'm dropping the promise API. I'd like to see us land the sync/async versions and then progress from there.

It feels a bit odd to land an implementation without the Promise API, I think we've tended to make sure to have cb/promise/sync all available when landing new filesystem features.

If we concentrated on recursive `opendir`, I think it might overall make the implementation easier, and we could support all three methods.

The promise version of `opendir` is just using `promisify`:

https://github.com/nodejs/node/blob/master/lib/internal/fs/promises.js#L857

And the logic is nicely encapsulated in `dir.js`:

https://github.com/nodejs/node/blob/master/lib/internal/fs/dir.js

I think basically, you could just add some recursive logic into this file (when you see a directory entry, recurse), and you'd immediately have support for the `cb` and Promise implementation.

---

Sorry for the slow response by the way, I've been a swamped at work (_feel free to private message me on Twitter, or email me, if you're ever held up on my feedback._)

> I think basically, you could just add some recursive logic into this file

My recent changes do exactly this (but only the sync part for now)! Next week i will work on the callback part and hopefully the promisify will work as well.

> It feels a bit odd to land an implementation without the Promise API,

I generally agree with this. @Ethan-Arrowood any chance we can get this in addition?
Yes definitely. I struggled to get the async solution during my first pass. I'll be giving it another shot soon when I can focus on it more and then the promise part should be easy to add on top

I got some form of the callback style working ( i think ). Going to keep hacking at this and see what the promise based version does.

In this thread there are comments about not reading all of the results into memory (and using a stream or an async iterator). Unfortunately the existing opendir does not function like this. Even the callback/async version will read the entire directory, and then return each `dirent` everytime `.read` is called. I have kept this behavior in this first pass. Maybe as I work on the promise part of this something will come to me. 

Interested to see other folk's thoughts on the currently implemented solution 🌟

Okay so while its still fresh on my mind, I met with @MoLow recently to see if we could figure this out. We got the code running on SmartOS and discovered that it within the result of `dirBinding.opendir`, the results had a returned type of `0`, which when passed to utilities calls like `getDirent` and `getDirents`, the `if (type === UV_DIRENT_UNKNOWN)` was resulting in true, and thus a `join(path, name)` was being triggered. This is problematic because my solution does a `join` operation _before_ passing things to `getDirent` so that the path of the `dirent` instance makes sense.

---

I got the `opendir` pieces working, but can't get `readdir` to work.

---

My next steps are to get access to the SmartOS machine from @nodejs/build . I know I can access, build, and run the code on that (since Moshe and I did it previously). Hopefully then I can debug the code and fix `readdir`.

Now with that i was able to fix what I think was the actual bug, `filepath` being used instead of `path` for `DirentFromStats`.

issue_context.title: Recursively list file paths in directory
issue_context.body:
<!--
Thank you for suggesting an idea to make Node.js better.

Please fill in as much of the template below as you're able.
-->

**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**
Please describe the problem you are trying to solve.

Recursively list file paths in a directory

**Describe the solution you'd like**
Please describe the desired behavior.

Dir structure like: 
```
| a /
| |- b /
| |   |- c /
| |   |    |- d.js
| |   |    |- e.js
| |   |- f.js
| |- g.js
```

Should return ['a/b/c/d.js', 'a/b/c/e.js', 'a/b/f.js', 'a/g.js']

**Describe alternatives you've considered**
Please describe alternative solutions or features you have considered.

Some public solutions that are synchronous and may be able to made faster:
- https://attacomsian.com/blog/nodejs-list-directory-files
- https://coderrocketfuel.com/article/recursively-list-all-the-files-in-a-directory-using-node-js
- https://stackoverflow.com/questions/26827920/nodejs-recursively-list-files-in-directory

---

I wrote a version of this using async/await and typescript [tweet](https://twitter.com/ArrowoodTech/status/1300236323412938753?s=20). Not tested much and needs to be extrapolated for general purpose use

If this something the community is interested in I'd be happy to contribute it!

Do we have to be strict about `typeof options.recursive === 'boolean'`, or we can allow any truthy/falsy value, similar to `options.withFileTypes`?

Not being strict with boolean type checks create issues where you also have to check `1`. I've worked on something similar and without introducing a breaking change, I had to add `Booelan(value)` to pass it. If in the future we move this function to C++, it would be a lot easier to validate the `truthy` of the value. So, I recommend being as strict as possible.
